q: In Taiwan's November 28, 2026, local elections, Kuomintang nominees or joint candidates formally endorsed by the Kuomintang and the Taiwan People's Party win at least 12 of the 22 mayoral and county magistrate posts (independents and candidates backed by the Taiwan People's Party alone do not count)
basis: The Kuomintang holds 13 or 14 of the 22 posts, so the question is whether it loses two or fewer. The party is running a joint candidate with the Taiwan People's Party for mayor of New Taipei, but the two parties ended their cooperation in Hsinchu County on September 6. The outcome would be an early signal of a Kuomintang victory in the 2028 presidential election (an external variable, 45 percent) and would prompt a fresh look at the odds of a U.S.-China bargain over Taiwan (brokered stability).
rs: Certified results from Taiwan's Central Election Commission
